whatIs.question: What is an implant?
whatIs.answer: A dental implant is an artificial root—usually made of biocompatible titanium—placed into the jawbone to replace a missing tooth root. It can be used to treat all kinds of tooth loss. After the implant fuses with the bone, porcelain teeth are attached to it using either a screw-retained or cemented method.

toWhom.question: Who can receive implants?
toWhom.answer: Dental implants can be applied to individuals with good overall health, who have completed adolescence, and who are considered suitable for implant treatment by a dentist.

doctorDiagnosis.question: In which cases does implant treatment depend on the dentist’s evaluation?
doctorDiagnosis.text: In the following cases, implant treatment depends on the dentist’s assessment:
list: Individuals whose bone development is not complete
People with alcohol or substance dependence
Chronic conditions such as hemophilia and high blood pressure

isHarmful.question: Is it harmful?
isHarmful.answer:
Prive Implant products are made from pure titanium with high biocompatibility. When applied correctly and maintained regularly, success rates of up to 98% have been reported.

As with any surgical procedure, implant treatment also carries potential risks. Your dentist will determine the healthiest option for you.

lifeSpan.question: How long do implants last?
lifeSpan.answer:
Implants interact with the bone and gums similarly to natural teeth. If regular oral care is neglected, gum problems can also occur around implants.

With proper oral hygiene and routine dental check-ups, implants can be used healthily for many years. Today, there are patients who still use implants placed 30 years ago.
